verses.sanskrit:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच।
              चिन्तयित्वा तदाश्चर्यं स्त्रिया प्रोक्तमशेषतः। विनिन्दन् स स्वमात्मानमागस्कृत इवाबभौ॥१॥
verses.english: Markandeya said : Continuously meditating upon that wonder, which the woman had told and reproaching himself very often, he appeared as if he was a criminal.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्तयानः स्वधर्मस्य सूक्ष्मां गतिमथाब्रवीत्। श्रद्दधानेन वै भाव्यं गच्छामि मिथिलामहम्॥२॥
verses.english: Thus meditating upon the fine way of virtue, he said, I should, indeed, respectfully agree to her speech; and, therefore, go at once to Mithila.
verses.bhavadeepa: चिन्तयित्वेति । आगोऽपराधः कृतमनेनेत्यागस्कृत : ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: कृतात्मा धर्मवित् तस्यां व्याधो निवसते किल। तं गच्छाम्यहमद्यैव धर्मं प्रष्टुं तपोधनम्॥३॥
verses.english: Surely there lives in that city a fowler, who possess a soul under complete control and who also is thoroughly versed in the principles of morality. This day I will go to him, who possesses wealth of asceticism in order to ask him about the principles of morality.

verses.sanskrit: इति सञ्चित्य मनसा श्रद्दधानः स्त्रिया वचः। बलाकाप्रत्ययेनासौ धर्म्यैश्च वचनैः शुभैः॥४॥
verses.english: Thus meditating in his mind and relying upon the statement of the woman, which was ensured by her knowledge of the death of the female crane, as also by her happy discourse bearing upon the principles of virtue, he (Kaushika), being filled with curiosity.

verses.sanskrit: सम्प्रतस्थे स मिथिलां कौतुहलसमन्वितः। अतिक्रामन्नरण्यानि ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च॥५॥
verses.english: (He) departed to Mithila and crossed over forests, villages and cities. Then at last he came to Mithila, which was governed by king Janaka. The city was decorated with the flags hoisted by men of various creeds. It was echoed with the sound of sacrifices and festive celebrations. Also the city looked most beautiful.

verses.sanskrit: ततो जगाम मिथिलां जनकेन सुरक्षिताम्। धर्मसेतुसमाकीर्णां यज्ञोत्सववतीं शुभाम्॥६॥
गोपुराट्टालकवतीं हर्म्यप्राकारशोभनाम्। प्रविश्य नगरीं रम्यां विमानैर्बहुभिर्युताम्॥७॥
verses.english: Having entered that beautiful city, he saw that it was adorned with magnificent porches, buildings and splendid palaces, and protected on all sides by lofty walls and also filled with numberless cars.

verses.sanskrit: पण्यैश्च बहुभिर्युक्तां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। अश्वै रथैस्तथा नागैर्योधैश्च बहुभिर्युताम्॥८॥
verses.english: The city was traversed by several broad roads, lined with innumerable shops. It was also covered over with innumerable horses, cars, elephants and warriors.
verses.bhavadeepa: विमानैः साप्तभौमिकगृहैः ॥७॥

verses.sanskrit: हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णां नित्योत्सवसमाकुलाम्। सोऽपश्यद्बहुवृत्तान्तां ब्राह्मणः समतिक्रमन्॥९॥
verses.english: The Brahmana saw the town full of men, who were enjoying health and cheer and were always engaged in the celebration of festivities; as also he saw there various other things.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मव्याधमपृच्छच्च स चास्य कथितो द्विजैः। अपश्यत् तत्र गत्वा तं सूनामध्ये व्यवस्थितम्॥१०॥
verses.english: Having entered the city, he searched after the virtuous Fowler. Some regenerate persons pointed out to him the place, where he repaired and saw the Fowler seated in the midst of a butcher's yard.

verses.sanskrit: मार्गमाहिषमांसानि विक्रीणन्तं तपस्विनम्। आकुलत्वाच्च क्रेतॄणामेकान्ते संस्थितो द्विजः॥११॥
verses.english: The twice-born person stood at a distant corner; for the fowler, devoted to asceticism, was then selling venison and the flesh of the buffalo; and a large number of buyers gathered round him in right earnest.
verses.bhavadeepa: सूना वधस्थानं तन्मध्ये ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: स तु ज्ञात्वा द्विजं प्राप्तं सहसा सम्भ्रमोत्थितः। आजगाम यतो विप्रः स्थित एकान्तदर्शने॥१२॥
verses.english: Understanding that the twice-born one had come to him, he (fowler) suddenly got up from his seat and went to the place, where the Brahmana was standing in seclusion.

verses.sanskrit:
व्याध उवाच।
              अभिवादये त्वां भगवन् स्वागतं ते द्विजोत्तम। अहं व्याधो हि भद्रं ते किं करोमि प्रशाधि माम्॥१३॥
verses.english: The Fowler said: O virtuous one, O foremost of the regenerate ones, I salute you. You are welcome! I am the fowler. Indeed, be you happy! Command me what I will do for you.

verses.sanskrit: एकपत्न्या यदुक्तोऽसि गच्छ त्वं मिथिलामिति। जानाम्येतदहं सर्वं यदर्थं त्वमिहागतः॥१४॥
verses.english: The words, that a woman told to you, viz., you go to Mithila, are all known to me. I know also with what object you have come here.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा च तस्य तद्वाक्यं स विप्रो भृशविस्मितः। द्वितीयमिदमाश्चर्यमित्यचिन्तयत द्विजः॥१५॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of his, the Brahmana became greatly astonished. The regenerate person went on meditating-Oh! this is the second marvel!

verses.sanskrit: अदेशस्थं हि ते स्थानमिति व्याधोऽब्रवीदिदम्। गृहं गच्छाव भगवन् यदि ते रोचतेऽनघ॥१६॥
verses.english: The fowler then addressed the Brahmana, saying-Indeed, you are now staying at a place, that is not at all proper for you. O holy one, O faultless one, should you like, let us go to my own abode.

verses.sanskrit:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच।
              बाढमित्येव तं विप्रो हृष्टो वचनमब्रवीत्। अग्रतस्तु द्विजं कृत्वा स जगाम गृहं प्रति॥१७॥
verses.english: Markandeya said : The Brahmana, highly gratified, addressed him, saying, "So be it". Making the Brahmana proceed before him, he (fowler) departed towards his own abode.
verses.bhavadeepa: अदेशस्थमयोग्यदेशस्थम् ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रविश्य च गृहं रम्यमासनेनाभिपूजितः। पाद्यमाचमनीयं च प्रतिगृह्य द्विजोत्तमः॥१८॥

व्याध उवाच।
              कुलोचितमिदं कर्म पितृपैतामहं परम्। वर्तमानस्य मे धर्मे स्वे मन्युं मा कृथा द्विज॥२०॥
verses.english: The Fowler said: This profession belongs to my race; and it has descended to me from my father and grandfather. O twice-born one, do not be sorry for the reason of my adopting the profession that belongs to my own family.
verses.bhavadeepa: न ग्लाति न ग्लानिं नयति ॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: विधात्रा विहितं पूर्वं कर्म स्वमनुपालयन्। प्रयत्नाच्च गुरू वृद्धौ शुश्रूषेऽहं द्विजोत्तम॥२१॥
verses.english: Fulfilling the duties of my own trade, to which I am already destined by the creator, I carefully devote myself, O best of the regenerate ones, to the service of my superiors as well as the old men.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यं वदे नाभ्यसूये यथाशक्ति ददानि च। देवतातिथिभृत्यानामवशिष्टेन वर्तये॥२२॥
verses.english: I always speak the truth; and I never envy other persons. As also I give away to the best of my power; and live upon what is left after the service of the gods, the guests and my own dependents.
verses.bhavadeepa: गुरू मातापितरौ ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: न कुत्सयाम्यहं किञ्चिन्न गर्हे बलवत्तरम्। कृतमन्वेति कर्तारं पुराकर्म द्विजोत्तम॥२३॥
verses.english: I never speak evil of anything; neither I hate anything, however great. O best of the twiceborn persons, the actions done in the past existence always follow the doer.
verses.bhavadeepa: नाभ्यसूये परगुणेषु दोषं नाविष्कुर्वे । वर्तये जीवामि ॥२२॥

verses.sanskrit: कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यमिह लोकस्य जीवनम्। दण्डनीतिस्त्रयी विद्या तेन लोको भवत्युत्त॥२४॥
verses.english: In this world the chief professions of men are agriculture, the rearing of cows and trade. But in the next world, the acquaintance in ethics and the three special branches of knowledge (the three Vedas) prove most conducive.
verses.bhavadeepa: कुत्सा विद्यमानदोषसङ्कीर्तनम् । गर्हा अविद्यमानदोषारोपः । पुराकृतं कर्मेति सम्बन्धः ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit: कर्म शूद्रे कृषिर्वैश्ये सङ्ग्रामः क्षत्रिये स्मृतः। ब्रह्मचर्यं तपो मन्त्राः सत्यं च ब्राह्मणे सदा॥२५॥
verses.english: Service of other three classes has been the fixed duty of the Shudra. Agriculture has been fixed for the Vaishyas; and fighting has been ordained for the Kshatriyas. The vow of Brahmacharya, devotion, repetition of the mantras and truthfulness are always to be observed by the Brahmanas.
verses.bhavadeepa: लोकः परलोकः ॥२४॥

verses.sanskrit: राजा प्रशास्ति धर्मेण स्वकर्मनिरताः प्रजाः। विकर्माणश्च ये केचित् तान् युनक्ति स्वकर्मसु॥२६॥
verses.english: The king should govern, in accordance with the dictates of virtue, the subjects, who always stick to their fixed profession. He should also appoint men to their own profession, who have really fallen from it.

verses.sanskrit: भेतव्यं हि सदा राज्ञां प्रजानामधिपा हि ते। वारयन्ति विकर्मस्थं नृपा मृगमिवेषुभिः॥२७॥
verses.english: The king should always be feared by his subjects; because he is their lord. The kings, again, should check their subject, who has gone away from his fixed profession, even as they restrain the deer by the arrows.

verses.sanskrit: जनकस्येह विप्रर्षे विकर्मस्थो न विद्यते। स्वकर्मनिरता वर्णाश्चत्वारोऽपि द्विजोत्तम॥२८॥
verses.english: O twice-born sage, O best of the Brahmanas, there is none here in the kingdom of king Janaka, who has fallen from his ordained duties. In fact, all the four classes strictly follow their respective duties.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सुखोपविष्टस्तं व्याधं वचनमब्रवीत्। कर्मैतद्वै न सदृशं भवतः प्रतिभाति मे। अनुतप्ये भृशं तात तव घोरेण कर्मणा॥२९॥
verses.english: Seated himself at his ease. Thereupon he addressed the fowler, saying, "It appears to me that this business is not really suitable to you. O father, I greatly regret that you should adopt such a dishonourable profession",

verses.sanskrit: स एष जनको राजा दुर्वृत्तमपिचेत् सुतम्। दण्ड्यं दण्डे निक्षिपति तथा न ग्लाति धार्मिकम्॥२९॥
verses.english: Seated himself at his ease. Thereupon he addressed the fowler, saying, "It appears to me that this business is not really suitable to you. O father, I greatly regret that you should adopt such a dishonourable profession",

verses.sanskrit: सुयुक्तचारो नृपतिः सर्वं धर्मेण पश्यति। श्रीश्च राज्यं च दण्डश्च क्षत्रियाणां द्विजोत्तम॥३०॥
verses.english: With the assistance of the spies appointed by him, he casts a virtuous look upon all things. O best of the regenerate ones, prosperity, kingdom and the power of inflicting punishment rest with the Kshatriyas.
verses.bhavadeepa: न ग्लाति न ग्लानिं नयति ॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: राजानो हि स्वधर्मेण श्रियमिच्छन्ति भूयसीम्। सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां त्राता राजा भवत्युत॥३१॥
verses.english: Indeed, the kings, practising their own special virtues, crave for immense prosperity. In fact, the king is the preserver of all the four classes.

verses.sanskrit: परेण हि हतान् ब्रह्मन् वराहमहिषानहम्। न स्वयं हन्मि विप्रर्षे विक्रीणामि सदा त्वहम्॥३२॥
verses.english: O regenerate one, I never slay the hogs and buffaloes myself. They are slain by others. O twice-born sage, only I always sell their flesh afterwards.

verses.sanskrit: न भक्षयामि मांसानि ऋतुगामी तथा ह्यहम्। सदोपवासी च तथा नक्तभोजी सदा द्विज॥३३॥
verses.english: I never eat flesh myself. Really I have an intercourse with my wife during her season. O twice-born one, I always fast during the day and eat only during the night.

verses.sanskrit: अशीलश्चापि पुरुषो भूत्वा भवति शीलवान्। प्राणिहिंसारतिश्चापि भवते धार्मिकः पुनः॥३४॥
verses.english: A person, being born bad, may be of good character. Again, he may turn out virtuous, even if he be a slayer of animals by birth or profession.

verses.sanskrit: अभिचारान्नरेन्द्राणां धर्मः सङ्कीर्यते महान्। अधर्मो वर्तते चापि सङ्कीर्यन्ते ततः प्रजाः॥३५॥
verses.english: Virtue diminishes in strength on account of the misconduct of the kings, and sin becomes predominant. Thereon the subjects grow less.

verses.sanskrit: भेरुण्डा वामनाः कुब्जाः स्थूलशीर्षास्तथैव च। क्लीबाश्चान्धाश्च बधिरा जायन्तेऽत्युच्चलोचनाः॥३६॥
verses.english: Then also the formidable monsters, dwarfs and those, who have crooked backs and wide heads and those, who have lost the power of procreation, the dead and blind persons as also those, who have their eye-sight paralysed, begin to take birth.
verses.bhavadeepa: अभिचारात् स्वैरगतेः ॥३५॥

verses.sanskrit: पार्थिवानामधर्मत्वात् प्रजानामभवः सदा। स एष राजा जनकः प्रजा धर्मेण पश्यति॥३७॥
verses.english: In consequence of the criminality of the rulers of the earth, the subjects undergo continuous harms. But Janaka is such a monarch, that he looks upon his subjects with virtuous eyes.
verses.bhavadeepa: भेरुण्डाः भयानकाः ॥३६॥

verses.sanskrit: अनुगृह्णन् प्रजाः सर्वाः स्वधर्मनिरताः सदा। ये चैव मां प्रशंसन्ति ये च निन्दन्ति मानवाः॥३८॥
verses.english: He is ever kind to all his subjects, who perform their fixed duties. As for myself, those who praise me or those men who blame me, all of them I satisfy with deeds well done.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वान् सुपरिणीतेन कर्मणा तोषयाम्यहम्। ये जीवन्ति स्वधर्मेण संयुञ्जन्ति च पार्थिवाः॥३९॥
verses.english: But those kings, who lead their lives in the strict observance of their duties and are ever busy (in the performance of honest deeds) and who can bear austerity and possess smartness and promptitude, never depend upon anything for their support.

verses.sanskrit: न किञ्चिदुपजीवन्ति दान्ता उत्थानशीलिनः। शक्त्याऽन्नदानं सततं तितिक्षा धर्मनित्यता॥४०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: सुपरिणीतेन साधुना ये संयुञ्जन्ति सम्यग्योगं सेनानिवेशं कुर्वन्ति त एव पार्थिवाः। अन्ये चोरा इत्यर्थः ॥३९॥

verses.sanskrit: यथार्हं प्रति पूजा च सर्वभूतेषु वै सदा। त्यागान्नान्यत्र मर्त्यानां गुणास्तिष्ठन्ति पूरुषे॥४१॥
verses.english: Giving away food incessantly to the best of one's power, patience and firm belief in virtue, necessary regard for all creatures always, these virtues are present only in that person, who has wholly abandoned the world (the worldly pleasures); but in none else.

verses.sanskrit: मृषा वादं परिहरेत् कुर्यात् प्रियमयाचितः। न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत्॥४२॥
verses.english: One should do away with falsehood. He should render good to all without being asked. He should never forsake virtue out of lust or anger or malice.

verses.sanskrit: प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च सञ्ज्वरेत्। न मुह्योदर्थकृच्छ्रेषु न च धर्मं परित्यजेत्॥४३॥
verses.english: One should not express unnatural joy at good fortune or succumb under calamities. He should not grow dispirited, when overpowered by poverty or forsake his virtue when so overpowered.
verses.bhavadeepa: संरम्भाद्भयात् ॥४२॥

verses.sanskrit: कर्म चेत्किञ्चिदन्यत् स्यादितरन्न तदाचरेत्। यत् कल्याणमभिध्यायेत् तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत्॥४४॥
verses.english: If on a certain occasion one commits a wrong, he should not commit it again. One should direct his soul to what contributes to the happiness of others.

verses.sanskrit: न पापे प्रतिपापः स्यात् साधुरेव सदा भवेत्। आत्मनैव हतः पापो यः पापं कर्तुमिच्छति॥४५॥
verses.english: There should be no wrong over wrong; rather one should deal honestly. The sinful person, who desires to commit a crime, is slain by himself.
verses.bhavadeepa: अन्यत् विपरीतं स्यात् इतरत् तादृशं द्वितीयं कल्याणमेवात्मनः परस्य चाभिध्यायेत् जानीयात् ॥४४॥

verses.sanskrit: कर्म चैतदसाधूनां वृजिनानामसाधुवत्। न धर्मोऽस्तीति मन्वानाः शुचीनवहसन्ति ये॥४६॥
verses.english: By committing a crime one becomes wicked and dishonest. Those who consider that there is no virtue or those, who laugh at the pure and good, these vicious men undoubtedly find decay in the long run. The wicked person daily grows flatulent, even as the leather bag inflated with wind.
verses.bhavadeepa: पापे पापिनि प्रतिपापः प्रतिपापी न स्यात् ॥४५॥

verses.sanskrit: अश्रद्दधाना धर्मस्य ते नश्यन्ति न संशयः। महादृतिरिवाध्मातः पापो भवति नित्यदा॥४७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: वृजिनानां व्यसनवताम् । असाधुश्चोरादिस्तद्वत् ॥४६॥

verses.sanskrit: मूढानामवलिप्तानामसारं भावितं भवेत्। दर्शयत्यन्तरात्मा तं दिवा रूपमिवांशुमान्॥४८॥
verses.english: The ideas of those, who are destitute of all sensibilities and who also are most worldly, are worthless. The inner soul points him out (as a fool), even as the sun discovers all features during the day.
verses.bhavadeepa: दृतिर्भस्त्रा आध्मातः सन्नसारोऽपि पुष्टो भवेत् ॥४७॥

verses.sanskrit: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया। अपि चेह मृजा हीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते॥४९॥
verses.english: The fool cannot shine in this world only by praising himself. Rather the learned man, even if he be dirty and anointed, shines gloriously in this world.
verses.bhavadeepa: तद्वन्मूढानां भावितं चिन्तितम् । अन्तरात्मैव तं मूढं दर्शयति मूढस्य मौढ्यमेव स्वरूपज्ञापकम् ॥४८॥

verses.sanskrit: अब्रुवन् कस्यच्चिन्निन्दामात्मापूजामवर्णयन्। न कश्चिद्गुणसम्पन्नः प्रकाशो भुवि दृश्यते॥५०॥
verses.english: He never speaks ill of any one; nor does he utter his own praise. No person is found on earth, who shines with all the excellent qualities.
verses.bhavadeepa: मृजा हीनः मलिनदेहः। श्रियेति पाठान्तरे स्पष्टोऽर्थः ॥४९॥

verses.sanskrit: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद्विपरिमुच्यते। न तत् कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात् परिमुच्यते॥५१॥
verses.english: The person, who repents for his sins, is freed from them. If one declares that he would not commit the sin again, he is delivered from committing a second one.
verses.bhavadeepa: मूढमतमाह अब्रुवन्निति ॥५०॥

verses.sanskrit: कर्मणा येन तेनेह पापाद्द्विजवरोत्तम। एवं श्रुतिरियं ब्रह्मन् धर्मेषु प्रतिदृश्यते॥५२॥
verses.english: O best and foremost of the Brahmanas, he may also be saved from sin by the performance of any one of the ordained acts. O Brahmana, this is Shruti, which may be referred to as one this relating to virtue.
verses.bhavadeepa: पापात् प्राक् कृतात् द्वितीयात् करिष्यमाणात् ॥५१॥

verses.sanskrit: पापान्यबुद्ध्वेह पुरा कृतानि प्राग्धर्मशीलोऽपि विहन्ति पश्चात्। धर्मो राजन्नुदते पूरुषाणां यत् कुर्वते पापमिह प्रमादात्॥५३॥
verses.english: A person, who was formerly virtuous, having committed sins out of ignorance, can destroy those sins afterwards. O monarch, the virtue of persons shines again (drives off all sins), if sins are committed out of mistake.
verses.bhavadeepa: कर्मणेति । येन तेनेति जपतपस्तीर्थाद्यन्यतमेन येन केनचिदपि पापात् ‘परिमुच्यत इत्यनुषज्यते । ’स ब्राह्मणः केन स्याद्येन स्यात्तेनेदृश एव स्यात्‘ इति श्रुतिर्हि धर्मेषु धर्मोत्पत्तिविषया । ज्ञानोत्पत्तौ त्वेक एव श्रवणादिमार्गो ’नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय' इति श्रूयते ॥५२॥

verses.sanskrit: पापं कृत्वा हि मन्येत नाहमस्मीति पूरुषः। तं तु देवाः प्रपश्यन्ति स्वस्यैवान्तरपूरुषः॥५४॥
verses.english: After having committed a sin, one should consider that he is no longer a man. The gods behold his sin, as also the monitor that is within him.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्राक् कृतानीति सम्बन्धः ॥५३॥

verses.sanskrit: चिकीर्षे देवकल्याणं श्रद्दधानोऽनसूयकः। वसनस्येव छिद्राणि साधूनां विवृणोति यः॥५५॥
verses.english: The person, who with piety and without detestation, hides the faults of the honest, like holes in his own garment surely desires to provide for the means of salvation.

verses.sanskrit: पापञ्चेत् पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते। मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः॥५६॥
verses.english: After having committed the sin, if a person really seeks salvation, he is delivered from all his sins, even as the moon looks bright after it has come out of the clouds.
verses.bhavadeepa: चिकीर्षेदिति यः । साधूनां छिद्राणि धनादिहीनतया रिक्तानि श्राद्धादीनि यः विवृणोति धनादिदानेन विवृणोति विशेषतः पिदधाति ॥५५॥

verses.sanskrit: यथाऽऽदित्यः समुद्यन् वै तमः पूर्वं व्यपोहति। एवं कल्याणमातिष्ठन् सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥५७॥
verses.english: Thus seeking salvation, a man is freed from all his sins, even as the sun, upon rising, displays its lustre after it has driven off all darkness.
verses.bhavadeepa: सः कल्याणं मोक्षोपायं कर्तुमिच्छेदेव । साधुसेवनजात् पुष्यान्मुमुक्षा उदेतीत्यर्थः ॥५६॥

verses.sanskrit: पापानां विद्ध्व्यधिष्ठानं लोभमेव द्विजोत्तम। लुब्धाः पापं व्यवस्यन्ति नरा नातिबहुश्रुताः॥५८॥
verses.english: O best of the twice-born ones, do you know that temptation forms the ground-work of all sins. Men, that are destitute of enough of knowledge, having been given to temptation, commit sins.
verses.bhavadeepa: यथेति । मुमुक्षा पापनाशपूर्विकैवोदेतीति भावः ॥५७॥

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मा धर्मरूपेण तृणैः कूपा इवावृताः। तेषां दमः पवित्राणि प्रलापा धर्मसंश्रिताः। सर्वं हि विद्यते तेषु शिष्टाचारः सुदुर्लभः॥५९॥
verses.english: Sinful persons hide themselves under the guise of virtue, even as the wells remain undiscovered on account of the grasses growing over and covering them. The selfcontrol, which they seem to possess, their holiness, their speeches regarding virtue, all these are witnessed in them. But good behaviours are hardly found in them.

verses.sanskrit:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच।
              स तु विप्रो महाप्राज्ञो धर्मव्याधमपृच्छत। शिष्टाचारं कथमहं विद्यामिति नरोत्तम॥६०॥
verses.english: Markandeya said : Indeed, that greatly wise Brahmana asked the virtuous flower, saying, "O foremost of men, how shall I know the the virtuous behaviours?"
verses.bhavadeepa: अधर्मा इति । लुब्धाः धर्मशून्या अपि धर्मस्य रूपमिव रूपं यस्य तेन दम्भेन आवृताः तेषां दम्भिनामम् । अत एव दम्भिनां साधूनां च विशेषानवगमात् तेषु दम्भिषु शिष्टाचारः सुदुर्लभः दुर्बोध इत्यर्थः ॥५९॥

verses.sanskrit: एतदिच्छामि भद्रं ते श्रोतुं धर्मभृतां वर। त्वत्तो महामते व्याध तद्ब्रवीहि यथातथम्॥६१॥
verses.english: O best of virtuous persons, you are blessed! I desire to hear this from you. O lofty-minded one, O Fowler, tell me the details of it truly.

verses.sanskrit:
व्याध उवाच।
              यज्ञो दानं तपो वेदाः सत्यं च द्विजसत्तम। पञ्चैतानि पवित्राणि शिष्टाचारेषु सर्वदा॥६२॥
verses.english: The Fowler said : O foremost of the regenerate ones, sacrifice, gift, austerity, the study of the Vedas and truthfulness, these five holy things are always noticed. in . virtuous conduct. over

verses.sanskrit: कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा दम्भं लोभमनार्जवम्। धर्ममित्येव सन्तुष्ठास्ते शिष्टाः शिष्टसम्मताः॥६३॥
verses.english: Having control desires, anger, haughtiness, avarice and wickedness, those who take pleasure in virtue because it is virtue, are, in the opinion of the honest and wise, really reckoned to be virtuous.
verses.bhavadeepa: शिष्टाचारमाह यज्ञ इति ॥६२॥

verses.sanskrit: न तेषां विद्यते वृत्तं यज्ञस्वाध्यायशीलिनाम्। आचारपालनं चैव द्वितीयं शिष्टलक्षणम्॥६४॥
verses.english: Those persons who perform sacrifices and are ever devoted to the study of Vedas, have no behaviours other than what are practised by the virtuous. Indeed good behaviours form the second attribute of the pious.
verses.bhavadeepa: शिष्टलक्षणमाह कामेति ॥६३॥

verses.sanskrit: गुरुशुश्रूषणं सत्यमक्रोधो दानमेव च। एतच्चतुष्टयं ब्रह्मन् शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा॥६५॥
verses.english: O Brahmana, rendering services to the superiors, truthfulness, worthlessness and gift, these four are ever present in those, who are really virtuous.
verses.bhavadeepa: वृत्तं वृतं स्वेच्छोपात्तमिति यावत् । ‘वृत्तोऽधीतेऽप्यतीतेति वर्तुलेऽपि मृते वृते’ इति मेदिनी ॥६४॥

verses.sanskrit: शिष्टाचारे मनः कृत्वा प्रतिष्ठाप्य च सर्वशः। यामयं लभते वृत्तिं सा न शक्या ह्यतोऽन्यथा॥६६॥
verses.english: Once can wholly obtain credit by directing the heart towards virtuous behaviours. This he gains only be practising the above four; Otherwise to gain this becomes impossible.

verses.sanskrit: वेदस्योपनिषत् सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः। दमस्योपनिषत् त्यागः शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा॥६७॥
verses.english: Truth constitutes the essence of the Vedas. Control over passions constitutes the essence of truth. And self-denial (refraining from the worldly enjoyments) forms the essence of selfcontrol. These attributes are always present in a virtuous conduct.
verses.bhavadeepa: अतोऽन्यथा गुरुशुश्रूषणाद्यभावे ॥६६॥

verses.sanskrit: ये तु धर्मानसूयन्ते बुद्धिमोहान्विता नराः। अपथा गच्छतां तेषामनुयाता च पीड्यते॥६८॥
verses.english: Those persons, who, being intelligent and full of delusions, hate these virtues, surely tread in the sinful path. The men who follow them fall in the abyss of decay.
verses.bhavadeepa: वेदस्येति । उपनिषद्रहस्यं सत्यं ब्रह्म तदज्ञाने वेदो निष्फल इत्यर्थः। एवं दमाभावे सत्यं नास्ति। त्यागाभावे दमोऽपि नास्तीत्यर्थः ॥६७॥

verses.sanskrit: ये तु शिष्टाः सुनियताः श्रुतित्यागपरायणाः। धर्मपन्थानमारूढाः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः॥६९॥
verses.english: They, who are virtuous and are devoted to the observance of the vows, to the Shrutis and to self-denial; and they who have ascended the paths of virtue and are engaged in speaking truth and observing virtues;
verses.bhavadeepa: अपथा अमार्गेण अनुयाता अनुगन्ता ॥६८॥

verses.sanskrit: नियच्छन्ति परां बुद्धिं शिष्टाचारान्विता जनाः। उपाध्यायमते युक्ताः स्थित्या धर्मार्थदार्शिनः॥७०॥
verses.english: They, who are endued with the virtuous behaviours; they, who follow the orders of the preceptors; and they, who minutely observe the import of the scriptures, obtain the highest intelligence.
verses.bhavadeepa: श्रुतिश्च त्यागश्च ते द्वे परमयनं स्थानं येषां ते श्रुतित्यागपरायणाः ॥६९॥

verses.sanskrit: नास्तिकान् भिन्नमर्यादान् क्रूरान्पापमतौ स्थितान्। त्यज तान् ज्ञानमाश्रित्य धार्मिकानुपसेव्य च॥७१॥
verses.english: Forsake the atheists, who are notorious, wicked and always entertain cruel ideas. Take shelter under knowledge and always worship those, that are virtuous.
verses.bhavadeepa: परां बुद्धिमात्माकारां वृत्तिमपि नियच्छन्ति निगृह्णन्ति परं वैराग्यवन्त इत्यर्थः ॥७०॥

verses.sanskrit: कामलोभग्रहाकीर्णां पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम्। नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि सन्तर॥७२॥
verses.english: By means of the boat of endurance you cross over that river, which is replete with such creatures as the desires and temptations. Its waters are the fine senses and the shoals found therein are the successive births.

verses.sanskrit: क्रमेण सञ्चितो धर्मो बुद्धियोगमयो महान्। शिष्टाचारे भवेत् साधू रागः शुक्लेव वाससि॥७३॥
verses.english: As great is virtue or as it consists in the practice of intelligence and yoga, it looks very beautiful, when acquired and added to a virtuous behaviour, like the dye on a white garment.

verses.sanskrit: आहिंसा सत्यवचनं सर्वभूतहितं परम्। अहिंसा परमो धर्मः स च सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः। सत्ये कृत्वा प्रतिष्ठां तु प्रवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तयः॥७४॥
verses.english: Absence of malice and truthfulness are most beneficial to all creatures. Absence of malice constitutes the chief virtue, which, again, is founded upon truth. Indeed, all our desirabilities find their scope, when they are all based upon truth.
verses.bhavadeepa: शिष्टाचारवति शुक्लपटोपमे योगधर्मः राग इव साधुर्भवेत् शुक्लेव । वेति इवार्थे । ‘व वा यथा तथैवैवम्’ इत्यमरः ॥७३॥

verses.sanskrit: सत्यमेव गरीयस्तु शिष्टाचारनिषेवितम्। आचारश्च सतां धर्मः सन्तश्चाचारलक्षणाः॥७५॥
verses.english: Truth is the supreme virtue, which is specially adopted by the the pious. Good behaviour forms the peculiar virtue of the honest and the wise. Those, that are holy, possess good conduct.
verses.bhavadeepa: अहिंसां सत्यं च स्तौति अहिंसेति । प्रतिष्ठां स्थैर्यम् ॥७४॥

verses.sanskrit: यो यथा प्रकृतिर्जन्तुः स स्वां प्रकृतिमश्नुते। पापात्मा क्रोधकामादीन् दोषानाप्नोत्यनात्मवान्॥७६॥
verses.english: Every creature frames principles of his own according to his inherent tendency. The vicious man, who can not restrain his own self, becomes subject to these vices, viz., desires, wrath and others.

verses.sanskrit: आरम्भो न्याययुक्तो यः स हि धर्म इति स्मृतः। अनाचारस्त्वधर्मेति एतच्छिष्टानुशासनम्॥७७॥
verses.english: It is an immortal maxim that justice constitutes virtue. The virtuous say that evil behaviours constitute sin.
verses.bhavadeepa: यो यथेत्यर्द्धं व्याचष्टे पापात्मेत्यादिना । अनात्मवान् अजितचित्तः ॥७६॥

verses.sanskrit: अक्रुद्ध्यन्तोऽनसूयन्तो निरहङ्कारमत्सराः। ऋजवः शमसम्पन्नाः शिष्टाचारा भवन्ति ते॥७८॥
verses.english: Those men are reckoned to be virtuous, who never show wrath, pride or haughtiness and malice or whose conduct is ever marked by simplicity and quiet due.

verses.sanskrit: त्रैविद्यवृद्धाः शुचयो वृत्तवन्तो मनस्विनः। गुरुशुश्रूषवो दान्ताः शिष्टाचारा भवन्त्युत॥७९॥
verses.english: Those again, are said to possess virtuous conduct, who carefully follow the rites laid down in the three Vedas; who are holy; who possess piety and sacred character; who serve the superiors; and who also have the power of restraining the self.
verses.bhavadeepa: अह‌ङ्कारो दर्पः । मत्सरः परदोषासाहष्णुत्वं तद्वर्जिताः । शिष्टं गुरुशास्त्रोक्तमाचरन्तः शिष्टाचाराः ॥७८॥

verses.sanskrit: तेषामहीनसत्त्वानां दुष्कराचारकर्मणाम्। स्वैः कर्मभिः सत्कृतानां घोरत्वं सम्प्रणश्यति॥८०॥
verses.english: The actions and behaviours of those great men are difficult of acquisition. The sins of those men, who are made pure by means of their own actions, die out of themselves.
verses.bhavadeepa: त्रैविद्यवृद्धाः तिस्रो विद्या ऋग्यजुःसामात्मिका यत्र स त्रिविद्यो यज्ञस्तत्र साधवस्त्रैविद्या याज्ञिकाः । वृत्तं शीलं तद्वन्तः । मनस्विनः जितचित्ताः ॥७९॥

verses.sanskrit: तं सदाचारमाश्चर्यं पुराणं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम्। धर्मं धर्मेण पश्यन्तः स्वर्गं यान्ति मनीषिणः॥८१॥
verses.english: This pious behaviour is most wonderful, ancient, inchangeable and eternal. The wise men's who with sanctity lead a virtuous life secure heaven.
verses.bhavadeepa: दुष्कराचारकर्मणामन्यैर्दुष्करः आचारः शीलं कर्म यज्ञादि येषां तेषाम् । घोरत्वं हिंसादिदोषवत्त्वम् ॥८०॥

verses.sanskrit: आस्तिका मानहीनाश्च द्विजातिजनपूजकाः। श्रुतवृत्तोपसम्पन्नाः सन्तः स्वर्गनिवासिनः॥८२॥
verses.english: The holy men, who are atheists, as also who are unaustentatious and who are respectful towards the degenerate persons and who, again, are familiar with the holy rites, are deserved to live in heaven.
verses.bhavadeepa: आश्चर्यमसतां दुरनुष्ठेयत्वात् । सदाचारं सद्भिराचीर्णं पुराणमनादिं शाश्वतमनवछिन्नं ध्रुवं नित्यमत्याज्यमित्यर्थः ॥८१॥

verses.sanskrit: वेदोक्तः परमो धर्मो धर्मशास्त्रेषु चापरः। शिष्टाचारश्च शिष्टानां त्रिविधं धर्मलक्षणम्। पारणं चापि विद्यानां तीर्थानामवगाहनम्॥८३॥
verses.english: The explanation of virtue is threefold. The first is called the supreme virtue, which is inculcated in the Vedas. The second is what is laid down in Dharmashastras. The third is called the honest behaviour, which is observed by the pious.

verses.sanskrit: क्षमा सत्यार्जवं शौचं सतामाचारदर्शनम्। सर्वभूतदयावन्तो आहिंसानिरताः सदा॥८४॥
verses.english: Crossing over (the ocean of) knowledge, the performance of ablutions in the places of pilgrimage, forgiveness, truthfulness, simplicity, sacredness are the characteristics of virtuous conduct.
verses.bhavadeepa: वेदोक्तोऽग्निहोत्रादिः धर्मशास्त्रोक्तः अष्टकाश्राद्धादिः । शिष्टाचारः होलकादिः । शिष्टानां तुष्टिरिति शेषः । तदुक्तमभियुक्तैः - ‘सतां हि सन्देहपदेषु वस्तुषु प्रमाणमन्तःकरणस्य वृत्तयः’ इति । अस्यापि शिष्टाचारे एवान्तर्भावात् त्रिविधमित्युक्तम् । पारणं समापनम् ॥८३॥

verses.sanskrit: परुषं च न भाषन्ते सदा सन्तो द्विजप्रियाः। शुभानामशुभानां च कर्मणां फलसञ्चये॥८५॥
verses.english: Those who, are king to all creatures and who are never malignant and who never speak ill of anybody, are always dear to the twice-born ones.

verses.sanskrit: विपाकमभिजानन्ति ते शिष्टाः शिष्टसम्मताः। न्यायोपेता गुणोपेताः सर्वलोकहितैषिणः॥८६॥
verses.english: Who are familiar with the results of good or evil actions, are reckoned by the wise to be virtuous. Again, those who are just and virtuous and well disposed towards all and who are honest and have obtained heaven, who possess sacred characters and constantly tread in the path of virtue.

verses.sanskrit: सन्तः स्वर्गजितः शुक्लाः सन्निविष्टाश्च सत्पथे। दातारः संविभक्तारो दीनानुग्रहकारिणः॥८७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: विपाकं क्रमेण पुण्यपापयोः क्षयम् । तेन पुण्यह्रासहेतुः सुखं नेष्टव्यं पापह्रसहेतुर्दुःखं सोढव्यमिति भावः । न्यायो युक्तिः । गुणाः शमादयस्तदुपेताः ॥८६॥

verses.sanskrit: सर्वपूज्याः श्रुतधनास्तथैव च तपस्विनः। सर्वभूतदयावन्तस्ते शिष्टाः शिष्टसम्मताः॥८८॥
verses.english: Who are liberal in gifts and unselfish, who show favour to the distressed and who are revered by all, who possess the wealth of knowledge, who are devotees and who are kind to all creatures, are virtuous according to the honest and wise.
verses.bhavadeepa: शुक्लाः हिंसाशून्यधर्मवन्तः सत्पथे ब्रह्ममार्गे संविभक्तारः कुटुम्बेषु ॥८७॥

verses.sanskrit: दीनशिष्टाः सुखाँल्लोकानाप्नुवन्तीह च श्रियम्। पीडया च कलत्रस्य भृत्यानां च समाहिताः॥८९॥
verses.english: The persons, who are charitable, secure prosperity in this world and abodes of happiness, in the next. The virtuous men, if approached and solicited by the honest and wise, give away alms to them with the best of his power, even at the denial of the comforts of his wife and dependents. Looking to their own interest and having an eye upon virtue and the ways of the world.
verses.bhavadeepa: श्रुतधनाः विद्याधनाः ॥८८॥

verses.sanskrit: अतिशक्त्या प्रयच्छन्ति सन्तः सद्भिः समागताः। लोकयात्रां च पश्यन्तो धर्ममात्महितानि च॥९०॥
एवं सन्तो वर्तमानास्त्वेधन्ते शाश्वतीः समाः। अहिंसा सत्यवचनमानृशंस्यमथार्जवम्॥९१॥
verses.english: The men, who thus practise virtue, obtain the greatest amount of virtue through eternal ages. Persons, who possess the attributes of truthfulness, abstention from injuring others, modestly and simplicity and who are not malicious and proud, who are mild and selfsacrificing, who have self-control and forbearance, intelligence and patience, who are kind towards all creatures and who are free from desires and malice, are said to be the witnesses of the world.

verses.sanskrit: अद्रोहो नाभिमानश्च ह्रीस्तितिक्षा दमः शमः। धीमन्तो धृतिमन्तश्च भूतानामनुकम्पकाः॥९२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: एधन्ते वर्द्धन्ते ॥९१॥

verses.sanskrit: अकामद्वेषसंयुक्तास्ते सन्तो लोकसाक्षिणः। त्रीण्येव तु सतामाहुः सन्तः पदमनुत्तमम्॥९३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: नाभिमानः निरभिमानः ॥९२॥

verses.sanskrit: न चैव द्रुह्येद्दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्। सर्वत्र च दयावन्तः सन्तः करुणवेदिनः॥९४॥
verses.english: These three are reckoned to constitute the highest way of the pious, viz., a man must not offend anybody. He must be charitable. Also he must speak the truth always. Those great men of highest virtue.
verses.bhavadeepa: सतां पदं पदनीयं प्रार्थनीयम् ॥९३॥

verses.sanskrit: गच्छन्तीह सुसन्तुष्टा धर्मपन्थानमुत्तमम्। शिष्टाचारा महात्मानो येषां धर्मः सुनिश्चितः॥९५॥
verses.english: Who are kind on all occasions and who are filled with compassion, obtain the greatest contentment and ascend the superior path of virtue; and whose acquisition of virtue is most certain.
verses.bhavadeepa: करुणाः करुणावन्तश्च ते वेदनशीलाश्च मत्वर्थीयोऽच् ॥९४॥

verses.sanskrit: अनसूया क्षमा शान्तिः सन्तोषः प्रियवादिता। कामक्रोधपरित्यागः शिष्टाचारनिषेवणम्॥९६॥
verses.english: Harmlessness, forgiveness, peacefulness, contentment, agreeable speech, giving away passions and excitements, the service of the virtuous characters and actions performed in accordance with the dictates of the Shastra constitute the superior path of the honest and the wise.

verses.sanskrit: कर्म च श्रुतसम्पन्नं सतां मार्गमनुत्तमम्। शिष्टाचारं निषेवन्ते नित्यं धर्ममनुव्रताः॥९७॥
प्रज्ञाप्रासादमारुह्य मुच्यन्ते महतो भयात्। प्रेक्षन्तो लोकवृत्तानि विविधानि द्विजोत्तम॥९८॥
verses.english: Those who constantly follow the path of virtue and daily worship the virtuous, can ascend the palace of knowledge. It is they only who are freed from that greatest terror (rebirth). O best of Brahmanas, it is they only who have the power of observing the several aspects of human nature.
verses.bhavadeepa: कर्म च कर्मैव । कर्मणेति गौडपाठे कर्मणा श्रुतेन च सम्पन्नमित्यर्थः ॥९७॥

verses.sanskrit: अतिपुण्यानि पापानि तानि द्विजवरोत्तम। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथाप्रज्ञं यथाश्रुतम्। शिष्टाचारगुणं ब्रह्मन् पुरस्कृत्य द्विजर्षभ॥९९॥
verses.english: O foremost of Brahmanas I have thus related to you all about the virtuous as well as the vicious, behaviours according to my own knowledge or as I have heard on the matter. O Brahmana, O foremost of the twice-born ones, I have done justice to the subject of virtuous conduct, which I had introduced.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रज्ञा ऋतम्भराख्या वस्तुयाथात्म्यविषयं ज्ञानं तदेव उच्चत्वात् प्रासादं भयात् संसारात् लोकानां वृत्तानि अतीतानागतादीनि ॥९८॥
